title: Claim Filing and Appeal Time Limits by Tier — Insulin Pump Program
content:
Each tier of the Insulin Pump Program carries four payer time limits, all counted in calendar days. A figure of 0 means the step does not exist on that tier.

| Tier | Timely filing of an original claim | Corrected claim after a CO-16 denial | First-level appeal | Second-level appeal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Insulin Pump Self-Pay Program | 0 (no payer claim is filed) | 0 (not applicable) | 0 (no payer appeal exists) | 0 (none) |
| Insulin Pump Commercial HMO Program | 90 days | 90 days | 180 days | 120 days |
| Insulin Pump Commercial PPO Program | 180 days | 180 days | 180 days | 120 days |
| Insulin Pump Medicare Advantage Program | 180 days | 180 days | 65 days | 0 (the plan forwards an upheld denial to the independent review entity automatically) |
| Insulin Pump Original Medicare Program | 365 days | 365 days | 120 days | 180 days |
| Insulin Pump Medicaid Program | 365 days | 365 days | 60 days | 120 days |

## What each limit counts from

1. **Timely filing** — the payer timely-filing limit for an original claim, in calendar days counted from the date of service (the ship date); 0 means no payer claim is filed on the tier.
2. **Corrected claim** — the window for submitting a corrected claim after an unprocessable (CO-16) denial, in calendar days counted from the posting date of that denial; 0 means not applicable.
3. **First-level appeal** — the window for filing the first-level appeal (commercial internal appeal, Medicare Advantage reconsideration, Medicare redetermination, Medicaid plan appeal), in calendar days counted from the posting date of the denial.
4. **Second-level appeal** — the window for filing the second-level appeal (commercial external review, Medicare QIC reconsideration, Medicaid state fair hearing), in calendar days counted from the posting date of the first-level appeal decision; 0 means there is no customer-filed second level (self-pay: none; Medicare Advantage: the plan forwards an upheld denial to the independent review entity automatically).

## Points of comparison

- The Commercial HMO tier has the shortest filing limit, 90 days, and the Original Medicare and Medicaid tiers the longest, 365 days.
- The Medicare Advantage tier has a 65-day first-level window and no customer-filed second level; the Medicaid tier has the shortest first-level window, 60 days.
- On every insured tier the corrected-claim window equals that tier's timely-filing figure.
